name: Federal Zionism
summary: Federal Zionism applies federalism to Israel: it would turn the state into a federation of cantons with Jewish-majority, Arab-majority and Druze-majority units under one constitution that guarantees everyone's rights. It keeps the Zionist aim of Jewish self-determination while giving Arabs and Palestinians self-rule and citizenship, with security and foreign affairs held centrally. It is a proposal on state structure and says little about economics or social policy.
scope: The mainstream of the strand today, the Federation Movement's cantonal plan (about 30 cantons across Israel and the West Bank, Gaza excluded), with its precursors, Ihud and Judah Magnes's binational federal ideas and Daniel Elazar's federal analyses. The movement is small and has no party endorsement, so most statements outside state structure, citizenship, settlements and security are unaddressed and answered low.

keyFigures.name: Judah Leon Magnes
keyFigures.role: American Reform rabbi who wrote most of Ihud's platform for a binational Palestine

keyFigures.name: Martin Buber
keyFigures.role: Co-founder of Ihud, which sought Arab-Jewish parity in a federative union

sources.author: The Federation Movement
sources.usedFor: The movement's own plan: 30 cantons, Cantons Council, single federal constitution, citizenship for West Bank residents, central security and foreign affairs, settlements kept in place.

sources.title: Federal Zionism
sources.author: Wikipedia
sources.usedFor: Definition of the strand, Cultural Zionist and Ihud roots, canton breakdown, borders, state structure, religion-secular caveat.

sources.title: Ihud
sources.author: Wikipedia
sources.usedFor: The Magnes-Buber binationalist platform: political parity, immigration tied to parity, communal districts, regional federation, rejection of partition.

sources.author: Daniel J. Elazar, Jerusalem Center for Public Affairs

sources.title: The silence of the federated solution
sources.author: Ynetnews
sources.usedFor: Co-chair Emanuel Shahaf's account of the plan: citizenship, settlements, IDF as sole army, Gaza separate, refugees, no party endorsement.

universal-healthcare.rationale: The cantonal program leaves health and welfare to cantons and the federal level without stating a health policy, so no position can be read from it.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: The program and Ihud platform contain nothing on wage law; the movement is defined by constitutional structure, not labour policy.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Federal Zionism's sources are silent on economic systems, and nothing in a cantonal constitution implies a market or planning stance.

public-ownership.rationale: No source discusses ownership of utilities; Ihud-era Zionism had cooperative strands but the modern movement takes no stand.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Taxation is not addressed beyond the federal level handling macroeconomic policy, so adherents are not shown to hold a view.

unions-good.rationale: Neither the Federation Movement program nor the Ihud platform addresses labour unions; the label does not predict the answer.

property-fundamental.rationale: The federal constitution is meant to guarantee everyone's rights, but no source says property rights are central or overridable.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Business regulation is outside the sources; macroeconomic policy is only named as a federal task.

cut-welfare.rationale: No welfare position appears in the sources; the program only mentions rehabilitating refugee camps and Bedouin communities, which hints at spending but not a general stance.

worker-ownership.rationale: Economic ownership structures are not discussed by the movement; this is neither tied to nor ruled out by federalism.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Security is assigned to the federal government, but no source addresses surveillance trade-offs; adherents likely split between security and civil-liberty instincts.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Drug policy is unaddressed; as a cantonal matter it would plausibly vary by canton, and adherents have no shared line.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: The sources promise equal rights under a federal constitution but say nothing about speech limits.

strong-leader.rationale: A federal system with a Council of Cantons and double-majority rules is built around checks and shared power, which makes a gridlock-bypassing strongman unattractive; inferred, not stated.

state-harmful.rationale: The movement proposes a more elaborate state, a federation with constitution, cantonal governments and a federal government for security and foreign affairs.

limit-guns.rationale: Gun policy is unaddressed; the program only says the IDF and central government handle security, which does not settle civilian gun law.

empower-police-military.rationale: Policing is a cantonal function in the plan and security a federal one, but no source calls for more funding or authority.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Not addressed; if devolved to cantons it could differ by region, and the movement takes no line.

decide-locally.rationale: The program gives regional governments every function except foreign affairs and security, and cantons run education, policing, planning and housing.

rehabilitation.rationale: Penal philosophy is not discussed in the sources.

traditional-family.rationale: Family norms are left to each canton's own culture; no source states a stance, and secular and religious adherents would differ.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Not addressed; the plan lets cantons reflect their local populations, so a national position is not documented.

abortion-legal.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; cantonal control of social matters leaves it open.

more-religion-public.rationale: The program says citizens express religious identity within regional governments but makes no call for a larger public role; Wikipedia notes religious-secular tension as a risk.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: The movement's equal-rights goal is about Jews, Arabs and Druze, not redress of historical injustice, and the sources give no policy on it.

gender-social-construct.rationale: A philosophical question outside the sources, with no ideological connection to federalism.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: The plan has Jewish cantons maintaining ties with Diaspora Jewry while Arabs and Druze keep their own ties.

gradual-change.rationale: The movement proposes a sweeping constitutional restructuring but also says it could be reached unilaterally and step by step; no stance on gradualism in general.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Jewish immigration was tied to parity in Ihud's platform but the current movement is silent on levels; refugees' status is left to negotiation.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Shahaf says the EU and US would not oppose the plan and the program seeks international acceptance, but no source calls for strengthening the UN.

free-trade.rationale: Trade policy is not discussed, aside from federal macroeconomic responsibility.

nation-first.rationale: The plan is Israel-centred but seeks international legitimacy for settlements; no source states a nation-first line.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Foreign military action is outside the sources.

open-borders.rationale: Ihud tied immigration to economic absorption and parity, and a federation with a security role at the borders implies controlled borders; inferred.

limit-growth.rationale: Environmental economics are unaddressed in the sources.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Not addressed by the movement or its precursors.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: No source touches this; it is not related to the federal structure.

revolution-justified.rationale: The plan is a constitutional proposal even if possibly unilateral by Israeli law; Ihud was a parliamentary and reformist group, so violent revolution is not part of it.

experts-over-public.rationale: No source addresses technocracy; the federal design emphasizes democratic representation in a cantons council.

central-planning.rationale: Decentralization to cantons runs against central direction, though the economy is not discussed; inferred.

land-value-tax.rationale: No source links the cantonal plan to land taxation, so no position is inferable.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Estate taxation is outside the plan, which names only federal macroeconomic policy.

basic-income.rationale: No source mentions income guarantees; the plan's welfare content is limited to camp and Bedouin rehabilitation.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Not addressed beyond federal macroeconomic policy.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Industrial policy is not discussed; only macroeconomic policy is assigned to the federal level.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Ownership structure is not covered; the plan only promises settlements stay where they are.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: A constitutional federation of existing states and cantons presupposes ordinary money economy and no one in the sources proposes abolition; inferred.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Macroeconomic policy is assigned to the federal level, but nothing is said about central banks.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Not addressed; representation in the plan is territorial and by community, not occupational.

one-party-rule.rationale: The program calls for a federal constitution guaranteeing everyone's rights, a Cantons Council and agreement by most residents, which is incompatible with single-party rule.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: No source discusses monarchy; the republic-style federal proposal and Israel's existing parliamentary system imply a negative view.

democracy-best.rationale: The proposals are built around elected cantonal and federal bodies, an upper house and a shared constitution; Wikipedia describes equal rights and elected chambers.

direct-votes.rationale: Direct legislation is not part of any described plan, which relies on representative bodies.

workers-councils.rationale: Political power in the plan rests on cantons and a Knesset, not on workplace councils; inferred.

right-to-secede.rationale: The double-majority clause and single constitution show cantons are not meant to leave, though Gaza is separated and future two states are not precluded.

natural-rulers.rationale: Equal citizenship under one constitution implies rejection, though the sources never address the idea.

political-violence-never.rationale: Not addressed; adherents, as Zionists in a state with a military, accept state force and have no stated stance on political violence.

war-builds-character.rationale: A peace-oriented compromise movement is unlikely to endorse this; inferred, sources silent.

separate-church-state.rationale: Wikipedia says federation could deepen religious-secular divisions and the program leaves religion to cantons; no stated line.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: A single secular federal constitution agreed by Jews, Arabs and Druze cannot be scripture-based; inferred.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Security is a federal government function and the IDF the sole military force in the plan.

military-superiority.rationale: The plan keeps security with a central government and the IDF as the only military force, implying maintained defence capacity, but no source discusses superiority.

ethnic-nation.rationale: The plan builds a state of Jews, Arabs and Druze under one constitution, though Jewish cantons keep a Jewish majority.

equal-outcomes.rationale: The plan seeks equal rights and some rehabilitation spending, not equal outcomes.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Not addressed; cantons grant local autonomy to Arab and Druze majorities but not on indigenous grounds.

colonial-reparations.rationale: The sources never take up reparations; the plan's only redress talk is rehabilitation of camps.

civilizational-union.rationale: Ihud imagined a regional federation including Palestine, but the modern movement rejects unification by religion or civilization; inferred and mixed.

duties-before-rights.rationale: The program centres on a constitution guaranteeing the rights of all, not subordinating rights to communal duties.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Environmental philosophy appears in none of the sources on this strand.

limit-population.rationale: Not addressed; demography matters to Zionists but only via Jewish majority, not population limits.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Not addressed; a modern state project implies no such view.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Technological disruption is not a theme of Ihud or the Federation Movement.

human-enhancement.rationale: Bioethics is outside the strand's documents, so no stance is recorded.

algorithmic-government.rationale: The plan relies on elected cantonal and federal bodies and says nothing on automating decisions.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: Digital privacy is not addressed; the plan mentions security only as a federal task.

restore-past-order.rationale: The plan is a new constitutional order, not a restoration, though Ihud-style pluralism is sometimes framed as a return to early Zionist ideas.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Shahaf pitches the plan as a pragmatic solution to demography and settlements rather than an ideological one; inferred from his statements.

direct-action.rationale: The movement proposes a constitutional redesign pursued through politics, with a possibly unilateral Israeli legal route (Shahaf), not street direct action.

means-match-ends.rationale: The sources describe a constitutional end-state but do not discuss whether methods must mirror it.

return-to-foraging.rationale: A movement designing cantons and a federal government within a modern state has no connection to this; inferred.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: A federation with distinct federal and cantonal functions presupposes specialization; inferred.

production-for-use.rationale: Economic motive is not discussed in the program or in the Ihud platform.

profit-exploitation.rationale: A Marxian claim on profit has no counterpart in Zionist federal writings, which are silent on class.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Inferred from the plan's equal citizenship under a federal constitution; class politics is outside the plan.

collective-farming.rationale: Not addressed; kibbutz traditions exist in Zionism but the program says nothing.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: The strand explains conflict by competing national claims, not by capitalism, but never discusses the thesis directly.

taxation-theft.rationale: A federal government with fiscal and macroeconomic powers presupposes taxation; inferred.

individual-rights-only.rationale: The plan protects individual rights through a constitution but organizes the state by national communities (Jewish, Arab, Druze cantons), giving group-based territorial self-rule.

conscription.rationale: Israel has conscription, but the program only says security is federal; nothing on conscription policy.

exit-over-voice.rationale: The plan's emphasis is on voting and representation in a Cantons Council and constitution, not exit.

state-as-business.rationale: Not stated; the constitutional-rights framing treats citizens as members rather than customers; inferred.

positive-liberty.rationale: Not addressed beyond rights guarantees and rehabilitation of camps.

media-academia-power.rationale: No source addresses media or university influence.

hereditarian-race.rationale: A movement built on equal citizenship of Jews, Arabs and Druze has no racial hierarchy; inferred, not stated.

organic-representation.rationale: Representation in the plan is territorial and electoral, via the Knesset and Cantons Council, not by family or trade bodies.

total-state.rationale: Regional governments handle all functions except security and foreign affairs under a rights constitution, a decentralised not total design.

national-rebirth.rationale: Classical Zionism spoke of national renewal, but the federal strand is about institutional accommodation; no stance in the sources.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Some federal Zionist thinking stresses protecting Jewish self-determination in a defined area rather than adding territory, per Wikipedia, and Gaza is left out.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Alien to a constitutional federation; inferred.

bound-labor.rationale: Alien to a modern rights-based federation; inferred.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Epistemology is outside the strand's sources.

universal-morality.rationale: The sources do not discuss moral philosophy, and Ihud's religious and secular members would differ.

single-common-good.rationale: The federation exists to balance distinct communities with different majorities, through a double-majority clause and a cantons council, rather than pursuing one common good.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Federal Zionism is a Zionist position that reconceives Israel as a federal nation-state; the aim is protecting Jewish self-determination in Jewish-majority cantons.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: The program keeps Jewish ties to the Diaspora and does not touch the Law of Return; Zionists would typically keep it, but the sources are silent, and Ihud tied immigration to parity.

revive-national-language.rationale: Hebrew's revival is settled history; the sources say nothing on reviving other languages.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Firm governance is not covered by the plan, which concerns territorial self-rule.

school-vouchers.rationale: Education is a cantonal function in the plan, but no source takes a view on vouchers.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Not addressed beyond federal macroeconomic policy.

economic-freedom.rationale: The plan makes no claim linking political and economic liberty.

rule-by-example.rationale: The plan relies on constitutional rules and institutions, not rulers' example; inferred.

national-self-determination.rationale: Wikipedia describes the strand as protecting Jewish self-determination, with sovereign divisions for Arab and Palestinian-majority areas too, which extends self-determination to both peoples.

force-without-un.rationale: Foreign military action is outside the plan, which covers internal structure and security as a federal task.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Not addressed; Ihud included religious figures such as Magnes and Buber while others are secular.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: The plan would make West Bank Palestinians citizens, but welfare entitlement rules are not stated.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Welfare conditionality is not discussed anywhere in the sources.

class-collaboration.rationale: Labour relations are not part of the cantonal plan or the Ihud platform.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Not addressed; a state project that values Jewish culture cantons implies opposition.

dominated-front.rationale: Not addressed; the movement seeks acceptance from the EU and US, not a front against the West.

workers-nation.rationale: The sources organize politics by national community, not working class, but never address workers' organization.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: A rights constitution for all residents implies equal roles, though religious adherents would differ and the sources are silent.

ban-interest.rationale: Not addressed; a modern federal economy implies ordinary credit.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: The program rejects segregation by recognising everyone as equal citizens under one constitution; cantons reflect local majorities but do not legally classify and separate by race.

state-class-instrument.rationale: A theory of the state as class tool is absent; the plan treats the state as a framework for two peoples.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Energy production is not addressed in the sources.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Not addressed; the plan lets Arabs and Druze keep their identities, which suggests no assimilation demand for communities.

elite-replacement.rationale: A conspiracy theory with no place in the sources; inferred.

proportional-representation.rationale: The plan creates a Cantons Council, with two seats per canton in one version, but the Knesset electoral system is not discussed.

national-mission.rationale: Not addressed; a defensive self-determination framing suggests no mission to export.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Feminist social theory is not discussed in the sources.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: The movement's pitch is structural, not about corruption, and the sources make no such claim.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Incompatible with a rights constitution for all; inferred.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Accountability for past abuses is not in the plan, though Ihud criticised violence against Arab civilians after 1948 (a weak hint only).

night-watchman-state.rationale: Cantons would run education, policing, planning and housing, more than a minimal state; inferred from the division of powers.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Opposed to the equal-citizenship model; inferred, though Jewish communal continuity concerns exist among some.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: The program recognises residents as equal citizens and promises a constitution that guarantees everyone's rights; Ihud demanded political parity.

socialism-one-country.rationale: A Marxist doctrinal question with no bearing on the strand.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Federal Zionists accept Jewish self-determination and keep settlements in place, so they would not call such states colonial projects as a rule, though critics do.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Cantonal self-government and community identities suggest differentiated arrangements; the sources do not discuss personal law.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Conversion law is not discussed; religion is left to regional governments.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: Not addressed; irrelevant to the movement, inferred disagree.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Education is cantonal; religion in schools is left open.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: A doctrinal question about socialist states, not covered by the sources.

consent-of-governed.rationale: The plan requires a single constitution agreed by most residents of Israel and the West Bank, so legitimacy rests on resident consent.

trade-surplus.rationale: Trade balance policy is not covered beyond federal macroeconomic policy.

population-transfer.rationale: Shahaf says Palestinians would receive Israeli citizenship and settlements would stay, with no expulsion, and the plan is built on mixed cantons.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: The sources contain no absolutist non-aggression principle; the plan keeps the IDF as the sole army.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: A social-Darwinist premise that the sources neither state nor reject.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Not addressed; adherents might support protecting the constitution but sources are silent.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Equal rights under a constitution protecting all peoples fits it, but the concept itself is not in the sources.

separated-powers.rationale: Federalism with a Knesset, Council of Cantons and cantonal governments divides power by design, and one proposal has a federal Supreme Court able to annul discriminatory local laws.

vanguard-party.rationale: Inferred from the plan's democratic federal constitution; revolutionary organisation is outside its scope.

priority-to-poor.rationale: The program calls for rehabilitating refugee camps and Bedouin communities but gives no general rule.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: Public housing is not discussed, though housing is a cantonal function.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Strike law is absent from the sources.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Poverty causation is not discussed; only refugee camp rehabilitation is mentioned.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: The federal premise is that Jewish, Arab and Druze communities need separate self-rule, which hints at concern about friction, but the movement also seeks one shared constitution.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Plan uses election and appointed bodies; lottery not mentioned.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: The constitution is meant to guarantee everyone's rights; inferred.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Price policy is outside the plan.

party-controls-media.rationale: Incompatible with a rights constitution; inferred.

party-commands-army.rationale: Inferred from the plan placing the IDF under the central government; party control of the army is not discussed.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: The plan grants West Bank Arabs Israeli citizenship on adopting the system, not after a long wait.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Pay of legislators is not covered by any source.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Party organization is not discussed; no party has endorsed the plan.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Ihud envisaged a federative union of the Middle East, though the modern movement keeps sovereignty with Israel's federation; the answer rests on the Ihud strand only.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Not stated; the plan puts security with the federal government, with no sign of presidential command.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Church governance is irrelevant to the documented plan.

clerical-rule.rationale: Inferred from the plan's single constitution shared by Jews, Arabs and Druze; religious authority is not discussed.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Not addressed; a state-building, army-retaining movement is unlikely to hold it.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Not addressed; rights-guaranteeing constitution implies disagree.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Executive tenure is not discussed; the plan is about federal structure.

recall-officials.rationale: Recall mechanisms are not part of the plan as described.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: The plan seeks US and EU acceptance but takes no stance on military alliances or troop deployments.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Not addressed; planning and housing are cantonal matters but no one proposes abolishing rentals.

people-in-arms.rationale: The plan names the IDF as the sole military, not an armed citizenry.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Early Zionist agrarian romanticism existed, but the federal strand's sources do not take it up.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Not addressed; the plan unites Israel and the West Bank under one federation but not on that ground.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: No source takes up populist views of the educated.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Not addressed directly, but Jewish, Arab and Druze cantons are each to keep their culture.

death-penalty.rationale: Capital punishment is not addressed in the sources.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Education is cantonal and no stance is given.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Education is cantonal but no curriculum position is given.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Not part of the plan's documents.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: The plan grants citizenship to West Bank residents, which is a territorial route, but descent rules for the Jewish population are left open.

minority-language-support.rationale: Cantons reflect local populations and Arabs and Druze keep cultural ties, so minority-language support in Arab and Druze cantons is plausible, but unstated.

religious-exemptions.rationale: The plan leaves religion to regional governments without discussing exemptions from general law.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Millian social theory is outside the sources.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: The strand seeks constitutional arrangements, not economic transformation, and never discusses the link.

constituent-assembly.rationale: The program says a single federal constitution should be agreed by most residents, and its content is still to be drafted, which implies a broadly representative drafting.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: A rights constitution implies disagree; the sources are silent.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Global aid duties are not discussed.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Nuclear policy is not part of the plan, and its documents mention only the IDF as the army.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Not addressed; the plan concerns the federal legislature and cantons, not the presidency.

central-bank-independence.rationale: The federal level handles macroeconomic policy but no source says who controls the central bank.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: The plan keeps all settlements in place and brings the West Bank under Israeli law rather than ceding it to a sovereign Palestine, though Gaza is separated.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: No source states a theory of property.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: A Marxist debate with no bearing on this strand.

collective-defense.rationale: Not addressed; the plan seeks EU and US acceptance but says nothing on alliances.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Shahaf suggests extending Israeli law and citizenship unilaterally to the West Bank and sees no lasting occupation under the federation, though the final constitution is to be agreed by residents.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Not addressed; religion is expressed within regional governments.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: The head of state's role is not described in the plan.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Not addressed; the double-majority clause protects the system without discussing force.

region-keeps-system.rationale: Cantons keep their own government, councils and local legislation while belonging to the federation, which is the same pattern at smaller scale.

sacred-ruler.rationale: No place in a rights-based federal constitution; inferred.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Tax design is outside the plan.

character-from-environment.rationale: Philosophical anthropology is not discussed in the sources.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: A federal constitution guaranteeing everyone's rights binds all authorities, including federal ones.

space-expansion.rationale: Space goals are unrelated to the documented strand.

mixed-constitution.rationale: The plan mixes a Knesset and a Cantons Council, but this is territorial federalism and not the classical mix of few and many.

leader-cult.rationale: Not part of any described plan; inferred.

equal-parenting.rationale: Family court policy is not covered by any source.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: A Marxist-Leninist doctrinal point irrelevant to the strand.

land-redistribution.rationale: Not addressed; the program keeps settlements in place, which cuts against takings.

refugee-return.rationale: The movement would arrange citizenship for refugees in their host countries through negotiation rather than return, and only rehabilitate camps in the territory.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: The plan claims no territory beyond Israel and the West Bank and leaves Gaza out; inferred.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Contradicts equal rights under the constitution; inferred.

common-currency.rationale: The plan assigns macroeconomic policy to the federal level but discusses no shared currency.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Not addressed; the plan unites different peoples in one federation, the opposite of kin-based union.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Cantons give Arab and Druze communities cultural self-government within a shared state, though Jews also keep their own state character, so the clause 'rather than a state of its own' fits only the Palestinians.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: Federal Zionism is a Zionist position; it seeks Jewish self-determination in a homeland, not only equal rights in diaspora countries.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: A theory of history not discussed in the strand's documents.

no-bailouts.rationale: Bailout policy is not covered, only federal macroeconomic policy is named.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: The plan's federal constitution guarantees everyone's rights and requires a double majority of population and cantons to change the system, which limits national majorities.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Gender quotas are not in the sources.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Not addressed; the plan seeks international integration and acceptance.

moral-incentives.rationale: Incentive design is outside the documents.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Equal citizenship under a rights constitution implies it, though titles are not discussed.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Not addressed; education is cantonal and cantons would teach their own communities' history.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Federal Zionism rests on equal rights and Arab sovereign divisions; inferred.

patriotic-education.rationale: Education is cantonal and the sources do not say whether schools should teach national loyalty.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Affirmative action is not discussed; the plan's equality goals are about national communities.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: A Marxist crisis theory question absent from the strand.

former-empire-influence.rationale: The plan covers only Israel and the West Bank, with no claim to influence over a former empire's regions.

delink-world-market.rationale: Not addressed; the plan seeks international legitimacy.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: A Leninist thesis unrelated to the strand's sources.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: A constitution guaranteeing equal rights for Jews, Arabs and Druze cannot allow arbitrary private discrimination as a principle, though this is inferred.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: The program centres on a federal constitution guaranteeing the rights of all, with a double-majority clause making it hard to change.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Mandate-era boundaries are not discussed in the plan, and Ihud's views on them are not recorded.

elective-rulers.rationale: The plan operates through elected federal and cantonal bodies; hereditary rule not discussed.

minority-veto.rationale: The double-majority clause gives cantons a collective say but not a veto for individuals or single minorities.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Doctrine on resisting rulers does not appear in the sources.

parliament-supreme.rationale: The system divides power between the Knesset, a Cantons Council, cantonal governments and a constitution, so parliament is not supreme.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Aristocratic duty is not part of the documents.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: A movement trying to shape a state's constitution does not recommend withdrawal; inferred.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: Critical theory of culture is absent from the strand.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: Gramscian hegemony theory is not discussed by the sources.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: An American history dispute with no link to the strand.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Monuments are not discussed in the sources.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: The plan proposes a Western-style federal constitution but the sources do not argue about whether institutions fit civilizations.

military-guardian-role.rationale: The plan puts the IDF under the central government for security without a political role; inferred.

paid-care-work.rationale: Care work policy is absent from the sources.

single-official-language.rationale: The plan has Jewish, Arab and Druze cantons keeping their own identities, which points toward multilingual institutions; inferred.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Land law is not discussed beyond leaving settlements in place.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Cultural criticism of consumption is not part of the strand.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Covert action is not discussed by the sources.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Not addressed; consent-based constitutional design points against coercion.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: NGO funding rules are not discussed.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Birth policy is not covered, though Ihud tied Jewish immigration to numerical parity with Arabs.

residents-only-property.rationale: Not addressed, though cantonal control of planning and housing could allow it.

democratic-peace.rationale: The sources do not take up international relations theory.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: A constitutional order agreed by residents implies a duty to follow its laws; inferred.

non-intervention.rationale: The sources do not discuss intervention in other states.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Transparency law is not in the plan's description.

local-production.rationale: Economic localism is not discussed, though cantons have local powers over planning.

informal-organisation.rationale: A federal constitution and formal institutions are the plan's means; inferred.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Not addressed, though Shahaf seeks international acceptance.

religious-nation.rationale: The plan defines one constitution for Jews, Arabs and Druze, so the federation is not defined by shared religion.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: The federal level handles macroeconomic policy and cantons local functions, but no source says how revenue is split.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: Employment law is outside the sources.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: The plan makes the IDF the sole military force under a central government responsible for security.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Not part of a constitutional federation; inferred.

open-government-data.rationale: Open data is not in the sources.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Not addressed; a pragmatic constitutional proposal implies disagree.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: The plan gives Arabs and Druze their own cantons and equal rights, not a majority economic monopoly; inferred.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: The plan divides the country into 30 cantons, 20 Jewish-majority, so a people is spread across many units, not merged into one.

local-essentials-public.rationale: Not addressed beyond local government functions.

municipal-property.rationale: The strand localizes government, not ownership, and never discusses municipal ownership.

confederal-coordination.rationale: The plan is a federation under a single constitution with a federal government, not a confederation of local assemblies whose delegates only coordinate.

person-over-state.rationale: The constitution is meant to guarantee everyone's rights, which suggests individuals are protected from the state, but the sources do not state the principle.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Not addressed; Ihud's leaders were religious thinkers, but the modern movement is silent.

dense-cities.rationale: Urban planning is not discussed beyond cantons holding planning powers.

racial-group-interests.rationale: The plan organizes a state around national communities but not races, and its constitution is meant for all.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Not addressed; security is a federal function.

language-defines-nation.rationale: The plan joins Jews, Arabs and Druze, who differ in language, but the sources do not define nations by language.

communal-electorates.rationale: Ihud's platform divided the country into districts on a communal basis, but the modern plan uses territorial cantons and a common constitution, not separate religious electorates.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: The sources do not claim foreign plots; the federal plan itself was presented as a way to avoid sanctions and keep territory together.

free-public-college.rationale: Tuition policy is not discussed, though education is a cantonal function.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: A movement that keeps the IDF as sole military does not endorse refusal; inferred.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: Fiscal rules are not discussed beyond federal macroeconomic policy.

sacred-nation.rationale: Not addressed; a pluralistic constitutional framing implies disagree.

immigrants-learn-language.rationale: Language rules for immigrants are not discussed.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: The plan lets Jewish, Arab and Druze citizens express religious identity in their cantons, but it does not discuss interpretation or legal precedence.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: The plan builds on elected bodies and a constitution; whether adherents would define democracy only procedurally is not stated, as they add rights guarantees.

internet-shutdowns.rationale: A rights constitution implies disagree; inferred.

women-suffrage.rationale: Equal citizenship and equal voting in federal and cantonal bodies is the plan's premise.

homestead-ownership.rationale: Settlements stay in place by negotiation and constitution, not by homestead claim; inferred.

defend-planned-state.rationale: A Trotskyist doctrinal question the strand does not engage.

indirect-election.rationale: The Cantons Council could be elected by cantons, and one proposal has an upper house elected from first-level subdivisions, but the statement is about higher offices generally.

national-church-status.rationale: Not discussed; the plan leaves religion to cantons.

minority-territorial-autonomy.rationale: The program creates about ten Arab-majority and one Druze-majority canton, each with its own government reflecting its population.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: The plan gives Jewish, Arab and Druze majority cantons their own governments and adds a Cantons Council and a double-majority rule so no side governs by simple majority alone.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: Cantons hold powers under a federal constitution that can be changed only with a demographic majority and a majority of cantons, so a national legislature cannot simply withdraw them.

disputed-territory-plebiscite.rationale: The cantonal plan is set by constitutional design, not by a local vote on sovereignty, and the sources give no plebiscite stance; Magnes-era binationalists were wary of majority votes in a mixed land.

keep-colonial-borders.rationale: The sources do not address colonial borders; the plan redraws internal cantons within the existing Mandate-era territory without taking a general stance.

simple-living.rationale: Federal Zionism is a proposal on state structure and says nothing on lifestyle ideals, so neutral is inferred.

restrict-indigenous-settlement.rationale: Inferred from the plan's single citizenship and equal rights for all, with settlements kept in place; it does not propose limits on settlement, but Ihud tied immigration to parity.

equal-conscription.rationale: The plan leaves security to the federal level without stating draft rules for women and men, so neutral is inferred.

extrajudicial-killing.rationale: Inferred from the plan's single constitution guaranteeing everyone's rights, which excludes killing without trial.

missingStatements.text: A country with two national communities should be organised as a federation of self-governing regions, each with its own government, under one shared constitution.
missingStatements.rationale: The Federation Movement's plan divides the territory into about 30 cantons with their own governments under one federal constitution.

missingStatements.text: Residents of territory under a state's control should be granted full citizenship of that state rather than live under indefinite military rule.
missingStatements.rationale: The plan applies Israeli law to the West Bank and offers Israeli citizenship to Palestinians who want it, as the movement's page and Shahaf's account both state.
missingStatements.declined: Specific to the Israeli-Palestinian case and largely covered by existing statements on land, citizenship and divided nations.

missingStatements.text: Changes to a country's system of government should require both a majority of the population and a majority of its regions.
missingStatements.rationale: The proposal has a double-majority clause requiring both a demographic majority and a majority of cantons to change the system.
missingStatements.declined: Specific to the Federation Movement's constitutional design; too narrow for the bank.

notes: Evidence comes mostly from one movement's website and press accounts, not from a founding text; Ihud and Magnes represent an earlier binational strand that rejected a Jewish state and partition, while the modern Federation Movement keeps Jewish self-determination. Canton counts differ across sources (about 20 Jewish and 10 Arab or Druze on the movement's page; 19, 9 and 2 on Wikipedia). Economics, religion and state, and social questions are not addressed by either strand.
